output.name: Sekar
output.myth: Sekar was a young one who wanted to go far north. He swam under the grey floes until the light turned blue. Orrun, who carries the islands on his back, felt the small one pass beneath him and said nothing, which for Orrun is a kind of blessing. Just short of the pole the Bride's White Kite hangs, where Tavo left her on a good-humoured wind, and Sekar swam past her too. At the top of the world he came to the place where Hesk winds every string, and he pushed his head against the reel to see if it would give. It did not. The tusk came out of him then, straight and white, the way a bone comes through a bad knee. Aun saw it and laughed and cut a line to see what would happen. That is how the spear went up. Skarún, the Hawk Ennu made against the gulls, watches from the north-east and says the tusk is only a tooth that got ideas. The young ones say it is the way north. Both are right, so both fly him on windy days.
output.finding: Find the Bride's White Kite, Sóleth, and from her go one hand-span, about 18°, straight south, where the Straight Spear lies.
